intuition.text: Mira's escort positions behave like marks painted on a board she carries. Turning her rotates the whole board, even while her feet stay still. A guard far from her has farther to travel for the same change of heading. Cheap target geometry can therefore demand expensive movement.
intuition.situation: A ceremonial escort can keep a recognisable shape in an open court if its leader turns gently. Before using the same arrangement for a quick pivot, check the movement demanded of the guards.

example.name: Mira's Lantern Court pivot
example.description: Mira halts in Lantern Court with an escort slot behind each shoulder. Each offset uses {spacing} units along both of her local axes, and her scripted turn lasts {turnDuration} seconds. Rings show destinations; the chart checks the speed needed to reach successive samples against a {speedLimit} units/s guard budget. The reference turn lasts {fastTurnDuration} seconds. The full scene separately uses Arrive to move guards towards these targets; this study isolates the fixed-slot geometry.

steps.title: Keep offsets in Mira's coordinates
steps.text: The engine makes a wedge for {members} members, then measures it from its leading slot. Mira occupies that origin, with escort offsets spaced {spacing} units along her local axes. Cache these offsets: a turn changes their world positions, not the pattern.

steps.title: Let the leader determine the frame
steps.text: The study-local schedule changes Mira's heading towards {turnDegrees} degrees over {turnDuration} seconds. The engine's advanceFormation copies her position and heading into the fixed formation without moderation. Her current heading is {angle} degrees.

steps.title: Rotate, then translate each offset
steps.text: slotPosition rotates each offset into Mira's forward and sideways directions, then adds her position. The escort targets stay behind her and {orbitRadius} units away throughout the pivot; the worked step shows the coordinate arithmetic.

steps.title: Check the movement the targets demand
steps.text: The local measurement compares each target with its preceding sample. The largest displacement is {displacement} units over {timeStep} seconds, requiring at least {requiredSpeed} units/s to reach the selected target. The budget is {speedLimit} units/s: {speedStatus}. An excessive request is reported without slowing Mira or clipping the destinations.

pseudocode.ordinary:
centred = patternSlots("wedge", members, spacing)
// Measure every offset from the leader at the wedge's tip.
offsets = centred.map(slot => slot - centred[0])
formation = fixedFormation(offsets, leader = Mira)

progress = clamp((step - turnStart) / turnSteps, 0, 1)
angle = turnDegrees * pi / 180 * progress
Mira.heading = (cosine(angle), sine(angle))
formation = advanceFormation(formation, [Mira], null, timeStep)

targets = offsets.map((offset, index) =>
  slotPosition(formation, index))

// Exclude Mira's own slot; the first sample has no displacement.
displacements = escortTargets - previousEscortTargets
requiredSpeed = max(length(displacement) / timeStep)
report(requiredSpeed, requiredSpeed > speedLimit)

visual.textEquivalent: Both escort targets stay behind Mira and {orbitRadius} units from her as they rotate with her heading. Their latest sweep requires {requiredSpeed} units/s against a guard budget of {speedLimit} units/s ({speedStatus}).

references.title: gdx-ai documentation · Formation Motion · Fixed Formations
references.supports: Leader-relative rigid slots need limits on leader turning and clearance for the whole group; this documentation explicitly says gdx-ai does not implement rigid fixed formations.

limits: This turn peaks at {peakSpeed} units/s against a {speedLimit} units/s guard budget: {runSpeedStatus}. Increasing spacing or shortening the pivot can make the targets unreachable even while Mira stays still.

Passing the sampled speed check does not establish physical feasibility. A curved journey is longer than its chord, and this schedule starts and stops turning abruptly; acceleration and turning limits still need attention.
The target generator never reads terrain. A clear location for Mira does not establish clearance for her escort, and keeping the offsets fixed gives the group no way to squeeze around a wall.

nearby.why: Use scalable formations when the escort's membership changes and a recipe must generate a new set of offsets. It solves a different problem from turning an existing set.
Use two-level formation steering when a separately controlled anchor should guide the pattern and individual guards need time and freedom to reach their slots.
